wins.text: Full-year 2025 net income increased to $21.3 billion with diluted EPS growing 17% YoY; ROTCE reached 15%, up from 8% in Q4 2020
Returned $23 billion of capital to shareholders in 2025, including $18 billion in buybacks and a 13% dividend increase; repurchased $5 billion in Q4 alone
Average loans grew $49.4 billion or 5% YoY; period-end loans grew 5% in Q4, strongest linked-quarter growth since Q1 2020; auto loan balances up 19% YoY, credit card balances up 6% YoY
2026 NII guided to ~$50 billion vs. $47.5 billion in 2025, implying ~5% growth; NII ex-markets guided to ~$48 billion vs. $46.7 billion in 2025
Wealth and Investment Management revenue up 10% YoY; investment advisory fees and brokerage commissions up 8% YoY; full-year investment banking fees up 11% YoY; markets revenue up 7% YoY in Q4

risks.text: 2026 noninterest expense guided to ~$55.7 billion, up from $54.8 billion in 2025, driven by ~$1.1 billion incremental technology spend, ~$800 million in other investments, and ~$800 million in merit/comp increases, partially offset by $2.4 billion in gross efficiency saves
Commercial real estate office portfolio continues to generate losses; CRE office allowance coverage ratio declined to 10.1%; management flagged additional losses could be 'lumpy'
NII headwind from 2-3 expected Fed rate cuts in 2026; lower short-term rates pressure variable-rate commercial loan yields; Q1 2026 NII ex-markets expected to decline due to 2 fewer calendar days

Potential credit card rate cap regulation flagged by analysts; management acknowledged it is 'too early to know' the impact and outcome is uncertain depending on administration or Congressional action

Share repurchases expected to be lower in 2026 as capital is redeployed into organic balance sheet growth; CET1 at 10.6%, above 10%-10.5% target range, with RWA growth consuming ~45 bps of capital in Q4

guidance_items.detail: 2026 total NII guided to ~$50 billion vs. $47.5 billion reported in 2025; NII ex-markets guided to ~$48 billion vs. $46.7 billion in 2025
Markets NII expected to grow to ~$2 billion in 2026, driven by lower short-term funding costs and balance sheet growth
Average loans and deposits each expected to grow mid-single digits from Q4 2025 to Q4 2026
2026 noninterest expense guided to ~$55.7 billion, up from $54.8 billion in 2025; Q1 personnel expenses seasonally ~$700 million higher
Medium-term ROTCE target of 17%-18% reaffirmed; CET1 target range of 10%-10.5% maintained; ~$2.4 billion gross expense saves expected in 2026

analyst_concerns_not_in_prepared: Potential credit card interest rate cap legislation and its impact on WFC's card growth strategy
Specific timeline commitment for achieving the 17%-18% ROTCE target (peers provide explicit timelines)
Capital allocation trade-off between lower-ROA markets/financing balance sheet growth and ROTCE dilution risk
